- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after recent spikes in history.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after high historical values, then underestimates as prices drop.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting lag in reacting to recent price drops.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks; often underestimates the depth of drops.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price behavior.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — overweights recent high values and underweights low values in the history window.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–3% for each day after a recent spike, especially if the prior 7–10 days show downward momentum.
- Model should incorporate a “reversion penalty” for forecasts that exceed the 30-day moving average by more than 2 standard deviations.
